accepted.question_text: For sets of reals, are the selection principles U_fin(Γ, Ω) and S_fin(Γ, Ω) equivalent, where Γ is the family of open γ-covers and Ω is the family of open ω-covers? If they are not equivalent, does the Hurewicz-type property U_fin(Γ, Γ) nevertheless imply S_fin(Γ, Ω)?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 ([24, Problems 1 and 2]). (1) Is Ufin(Γ, Ω) equivalent to Sfin(Γ, Ω)? (2) And if not, does Ufin(Γ, Γ) imply Sfin(Γ, Ω)?

Notes added in proof. Zdomskyy, in a series of recent works, settled (or partially settled) some of the problems mentioned in the paper, the answers being: “Yes” for Problem 5.1, “No” for Problem 8.6, and “Consistently yes” for Problem 11.2.

accepted.question_text: Construct, in ZFC and without extra set-theoretic hypotheses, general topological spaces, and also Lindelöf topological spaces, that witness non-implications among the classical selection properties shown in the paper's classification diagrams.

evidence.quote: Project 5.2 ([24, Problem 3]). Find, without extra hypotheses, (general) topological spaces that demonstrate non-implications among the classical properties. Do the same for Lindelöf topological spaces.

accepted.question_text: Let Z be the Cantor-like space of nondecreasing functions f in N^(N ∪ {∞}) such that whenever f(n) < ∞ one has f(n) < f(n+1), let Q be the dense set of eventually-∞ sequences q_s coming from increasing finite sequences s, let B = {f_α : α < b} be a <=*-unbounded b-scale of strictly increasing functions in N^N, and let H = B ∪ Q. Must H satisfy S_1(Γ, Γ), that is, for every sequence of open γ-covers of H can one choose one element from each cover so that the chosen family is again a γ-cover of H?
accepted.context_brief: The Bartoszyński-Tsaban set H and S1(Γ,Γ)

evidence.quote: Let B = {fα : α < b} ⊆ NN be a ≤∗-unbounded set of strictly increasing elements of NN which forms a b-scale (that is, for each α < β, fα ≤∗ fβ), and set H = B ∪ Q. In [6] it is proved that all finite powers of H satisfy Ufin(O, Γ). Problem 6.1 ([6, Problem 17], [57, Problem 2]). Does H satisfy S1(Γ, Γ)?
